proposed_record.reviewerRationale: Stage this as a distinct, current public demand and procurement-program record. The official release names the Defence Drone Initiative, its responsible Government of Canada actors, intended CAF and Canadian Coast Guard users, the RFSA marketplace mechanism, and six concrete initial capability areas. It is more specific and operational than the broader Defence Industrial Strategy records already in the map. The secondary article confirms how the development has been reported externally, while all canonical claims and requirement text are supported by official sources. Reviewers should preserve the public-demand caveat and may edit or merge it if a closer live demand source is discovered.

fieldEvidence.excerpt: National Defence states that the Defence Drone Initiative will accelerate the development, testing and production of Canadian uncrewed and autonomous systems for the Canadian Armed Forces and Canadian Coast Guard.

The official release says the RFSA enables qualified suppliers to compete for future testing, prototype development, limited acquisitions and potential production opportunities, while noting qualification does not necessarily result in a contract.

The release identifies initial support areas including low-cost tactical ISR drones, uncrewed ground logistics systems, uncrewed maritime surface and underwater systems, counter-drone interceptors, drone munitions and deep precision strike systems.
National Defence frames the initiative as strengthening domestic capacity, reducing critical supply-chain dependencies, and creating opportunities for Canadian companies, researchers and workers.
Independent reporting describes the DDI as a standing supplier marketplace and links its explanation back to the Government of Canada announcement and CanadaBuys registration path.

demandSource.title: Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace
demandSource.summary: The Defence Drone Initiative is a Government of Canada program and supplier-marketplace signal intended to accelerate Canadian uncrewed and autonomous systems for Canadian Armed Forces and Canadian Coast Guard needs. It establishes a public RFSA pathway for qualified suppliers to compete for future work in specified uncrewed, counter-drone, integration, testing and production areas.

requirements.title: Qualified marketplace for uncrewed and autonomous systems
requirements.problemStatement: Canada needs a public supplier-qualification pathway that can provide faster access to relevant uncrewed and autonomous system capabilities for Canadian Armed Forces and Canadian Coast Guard operational needs.
requirements.desiredEndState: Qualified suppliers can compete for future testing, prototype development, limited acquisition and potential production opportunities through the public Defence Drone Initiative marketplace.
requirements.publicCaveat: Public-source alignment only. This is not procurement eligibility, endorsement, customer interest, or a classified requirement.

requirements.title: Operational uncrewed systems across air, land and maritime domains
requirements.problemStatement: The initial public capability areas identify a need for low-cost ISR drones, land logistics systems, maritime surface and underwater systems, counter-drone interceptors, drone munitions and deep precision strike systems.
requirements.desiredEndState: Canadian defence and coast-guard users can evaluate and access deployable uncrewed and autonomous systems that address the initiative's published cross-domain operational capability areas.
requirements.publicCaveat: Public-source alignment only. This is not procurement eligibility, endorsement, customer interest, or a classified requirement.

requirements.title: Sovereign Canadian uncrewed systems capacity
requirements.problemStatement: Canada seeks to reduce critical supply-chain dependencies while making room for Canadian companies, researchers and workers to develop, test and produce uncrewed and autonomous capabilities.
requirements.desiredEndState: Canada strengthens domestic industrial capacity and sovereign access to uncrewed and autonomous systems that can transition from testing and operational feedback toward production.
requirements.publicCaveat: Public-source alignment only. This is not procurement eligibility, endorsement, customer interest, or a classified requirement.
